name: tixel
description: Tixel is the safe, fair way to buy and sell tickets to live events — concerts, festivals, sports, theatre, and comedy. Every ticket is verified to prevent fraud, sellers are identity-checked, and resale prices are capped near face value so fans never overpay. Browse real-time availability, buy instantly, or join a waitlist for sold-out events. Trusted by fans worldwide and partnered with leading venues, festivals, and promoters across the US, UK, and Australia.

tool.name: search_events
tool.title: Search events
tool.description: Find concerts, festivals, sports games, and shows available on the Tixel marketplace. Use for both specific queries ("Olivia Dean London", "Coldplay 2026") and broader exploration ("pop concerts in London this month"). Returns upcoming events; pass an event's tixelSlug to list_event_listings to fetch tickets. To restrict results to a specific city, pass the optional city_id parameter — call list_supported_cities to get the list of supported cities and their city_id values.

query.description: Free-text search across event title, artist names, and venue.

city_id.description: Restrict results to a single supported city, identified by its city_id. Get valid city_id values from the list_supported_cities tool.

tool.name: get_selling_options
tool.title: Find how to sell tickets
tool.description: Help a user who already owns tickets list (sell/resell) them on Tixel. Returns the best way to list for the ticketing company the tickets were bought from (e.g. Ticketmaster, Ticketek, DICE, Eventbrite) and a direct tixel.com link to that listing page, plus generic fallbacks (forwarding the confirmation email, uploading a PDF). If the user hasn't said where they bought their tickets, call without ticketing_company to get the full list of supported companies, then ask them. Prefer the recommended option; offer fallbacks if the user can't use it (e.g. no account access). Do not use for buying tickets — use search_events instead.

ticketing_company.description: Company the tickets were purchased from, as the user describes it (e.g. "Ticketmaster", "dice.fm", "Sydney Opera House"). Also accepts special events like "Burning Man".

tool.name: start_email_listing
tool.title: Start listing tickets from an email
tool.description: Begin listing (selling) a user's tickets on Tixel straight from their inbox. Returns a one-off Tixel scanner address (scanAlias). The host should then use its email connector to forward the user's original ticket confirmation email — including any PDF or ticket attachments — to that address, sent from the email account the tickets were bought with so Tixel can verify ownership. After forwarding, call check_listing_status with the returned sessionToken to track parsing and get the link to finish the listing. Use this when the user has a confirmation email or e-tickets and wants to sell them; use get_selling_options instead if they ask how selling works or bought from a ticketing company with a direct Tixel integration (e.g. Ticketmaster, Eventbrite).

tool.name: check_listing_status
tool.title: Check an email listing's progress
tool.description: Poll an email-listing session started with start_email_listing. Long-polls (up to ~25s) while Tixel scans the forwarded email, then returns the parse status, any detected tickets, and a continueUrl — the link the user opens to finish the listing on tixel.com. If isPending is true the email hasn't been read yet; wait a moment and call again with the same sessionToken. A status of "parsed", "ai_accepted", "links_sent" or "listed" means the tickets were recognised and continueUrl is ready; "parsing_error" or "ignored" means it couldn't be used.

_published_faq.name: How do I add tixel to Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor?

acceptedAnswer.text: Add tixel to Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor by connecting its remote MCP URL in each client's MCP settings. In Claude, add a custom connector. In ChatGPT, add an MCP app. In Cursor, add an MCP server under Settings. The MCP URL is https://mcp-v1.tixel.com/mcp.

_published_faq.name: Is tixel MCP ready for ChatGPT and Claude?

acceptedAnswer.text: As of October 6, 2026, tixel scores 90/100 on Manufact's MCP publishing checklist. The scan does not yet meet ChatGPT publishing checks and meets Claude publishing checks. Passing these checks does not guarantee marketplace approval.

_published_faq.name: How clear is tixel's MCP tool documentation?

acceptedAnswer.text: As of October 6, 2026, tixel scores 92/100 in Manufact's review of tool titles, descriptions, input and output schemas, and behavior annotations. The review covers 7 of 7 discovered tools. The quality score measures documentation clarity; runtime behavior and marketplace readiness require separate checks.

_published_faq.name: What tools does the tixel MCP server provide?

acceptedAnswer.text: tixel provides these MCP tools: search_events, list_event_listings, and get_listing_details.

_published_faq.name: What are the best alternatives to tixel?

acceptedAnswer.text: As of October 17, 2026, alternatives to tixel in commerce-shopping on the Manufact MCP catalog include EbooksDepository, ecoExperten Energieausweis, PHS Pallets, Promotion Pros Catalog, and RCO-A2A.
tixel does not require authentication. It is a public MCP endpoint you can connect without logging in.
tixel is developed by Tixel. It is listed as partner on the Claude connector directory.
